transcript: Soho Playhouse is presenting (un)conditional by Ali Keller, a potent 90 minutes about two married couples that are having intimacy issues. Like with a lot of relationship problems, the thing that's named isn't really the whole story, and there's a lot of other stuff going on underneath it. Although these couples are having very distinct problems, their lives come to overlap in unexpected and altogether stomach-churning ways. These are difficult characters — some are better at stating exactly what they mean than others, but they're all deeply flawed, and I didn't find any of them to be very likable. But regardless of how you feel about them, you get invested in their pursuits for reconciliation, which to put it lightly, is quite an uphill battle. The stakes are also heightened by the fact that one of the couples has a kid who's caught in the middle of a lot of this and becomes collateral damage. I thought this was a very craftily-structured play, and the entire piece unfolds with consistent intrigue and anticipation. If you like psychological and relationship pieces, there's a lot to chew on here — humans are complicated. With that, another program for my collection.
